newsitem.title: POLAND: SOCCER-DORTMUND THROUGH TO EUROPEAN CUP LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND THROUGH TO EUROPEAN CUP LAST EIGHT.

text.p: World Cup defender Juergen Kohler scored a late goal to help Borussia Dortmund draw 2-2 at Widzew Lodz on Wednesday and secure a place in the quarter-finals of the European Cup.
The draw, which kept the Germans alongside Atletico Madrid at the top of Group B of the Champions' League with 10 points, eliminated Widzew, who have four points.
Kohler scored in the 62nd minute with a well-timed tap-in from a corner kick and Borussia, seemingly content with a draw, played out time with Widzew running out of steam during the last 15 minutes.

But the German champions had to fight their way back after Widzew striker Jacek Dembinski scored twice within four minutes in the first half following Paul Lambert's opener for Borussia from 12 metres in the 13th minute.

In the 15th minute Dembinski headed in after a towering free-kick from about 35 metres. Four minutes later he found the net again, lofting a beautiful chip over the Dortmund defenders and goalkeeper Stefan Klos, who had advanced from his line.
Borussia did not create many solid scoring opportinites in the second half but controlled the pace of the game and neutralised Widzew's only real weapon, the counter-attack.
"We are happy with a 2-2 draw. It is a just result considering the course of the match," Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said.
Norwegian referee Rune Pedersen booked Dortmund's Andreas Moeller in the relatively foul-free match played on a water-logged field in a light drizzle.

Widzew Lodz - 1-Maciej Szczesny, 2-Miroslaw Szymkowiak (4-Zbigniew Wyciszkiewicz 56th), 3-Tomasz Lapinski, 5-Pawel Wojtala, 6-Marek Citko, 7-Radoslaw Michalski, 8-Jacek Dembinski, 10-Ryszard Czerwiec, 12-Slawomir Majak, 15-Daniel Bogusz, 17-Andrzej Michalczuk.
